core_obligations: Set up the diagram and suppose the property fails (proof lines 4750-4773): let xi be a minimal versal object over R; the tangent space is a k-vector space, the differential d-xi is k-linear and the action of the derivations of k is by addition, so the displayed diagram has a middle column exact in the middle; if the orbit condition fails there is a nonzero D in the kernel K of the differential which does not map to zero in the dual of m_R/m_R^2, so D(t) = 1 for some t in m_R.

Build the subring and its deformation theory (proof lines 4773-4795): let R' be the subring of elements annihilated by D; since D(t) = 1 the map R' -> k is surjective, the kernel m_{R'} contains m_R^2, and consequently R'/m_R^2 tensor over k with k[epsilon] maps isomorphically to R/m_R^2, giving in particular a map R/m_R^2 -> R'/m_R^2.

Contradict minimality (proof lines 4797-4828): choose morphisms xi -> y over R -> R/m_R^2, y -> x over R/m_R^2 -> R'/m_R^2 and y -> x_epsilon over R/m_R^2 -> k[epsilon]; the axioms of a category cofibred in groupoids give the displayed commutative diagram, and since D lies in the kernel the object x_epsilon is trivial, so the lifting lemma produces a morphism x -> y; the corresponding ring map R'/m_R^2 -> R/m_R^2 is not surjective because of the strict inequality of lengths, which contradicts the minimality of xi over R, so such a D cannot exist.
proof_roadmap: Interpret the failure of the orbit condition as the existence of a nonzero derivation in the kernel of the differential which is nontrivial on the cotangent space.
Cut out the subring on which that derivation vanishes and control the deformation situation modulo the square of the maximal ideal.
Use the triviality of the induced deformation along k[epsilon] to lift a morphism, and contradict the minimality of the versal object.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that a predeformation category satisfying (S2) with a versal formal object has a minimal versal formal object satisfying the orbit condition (statement lines 4743-4748). The proof (proof lines 4750-4834) interprets the failure of the condition through a derivation D in the kernel of the differential, cuts out the subring on which D vanishes, and uses the resulting nonsurjective ring map to contradict the minimality of the versal object. H3: an original reduction producing a nonsurjective descent and a contradiction with minimality, written out in full.
